datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent along the Komadugu Gana River, Bursari & Tarmua Local Government Area, Nigeria as of 15 September 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240902NGA, GDACS ID: 1102720 This map illustrates satellite-detected water extent along the Komadugu Gana River in Bursari & Tarmua Local Governments in Yobe State, Nigeria as observed from a Pleiades image acquired on 15 September 2024 at 10:38 local time. Within the cloud free analysed areas of about 120 km², a total of about 40 km² of lands appear to be affected with flood waters. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extent-along-the-komadugu-gana-river-bursari-tarmua-local-government-area-nigeria-as]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed Pleiades satellite imagery acquired on 15 September 2024 over the Komadugu Gana River region, comparing cloud-free areas to detect changes in water extent and delineate flood inundation boundaries. The resulting water extent polygons were vectorized and attributed with area measurements in square meters and hectares, representing observed flood hazard extent at a single point in time.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis using Pleiades sensor data to detect and delineate water extent and flood inundation areas through multi-temporal image comparison
